name: How do I know whether to renovate an existing office or start over with a full build-out?

mainEntity.name: When is it smarter to reuse an existing office layout instead of doing a full office build-out?
mainEntity.text: When is it smarter to reuse an existing office layout instead of doing a full office build-out?

acceptedAnswer.text: The decision between renovating an existing office and doing a full build-out depends on how much the current space already matches the tenant’s needs. If the layout is close, systems are in good shape, and the finish level is acceptable, selective renovation can save money and shorten the timeline. If the space has poor workflow, outdated systems, or a brand presentation that does not fit the business, a full build-out may produce better long-term value even if it costs more upfront. In Los Angeles-area markets, this choice is often influenced by lease term, landlord allowance, and how much time the tenant has before move-in. A costed test-fit or feasibility review is the best way to compare the options before committing.
acceptedAnswer.description: Reuse makes sense when the current layout is close to the new needs, the systems are in good condition, and code compliance is manageable. A full build-out is usually better when the space needs major layout changes, system upgrades, or a higher-end brand experience.
